customConcept.name: McDonald's franchise
customConcept.blurb: A drive-thru, a dining room nobody sits in for long, and a rulebook the size of a phone directory. You own the operation; McDonald's owns the land, the brand and a slice of every dollar.

state.circumstances: You bought this McDonald's from a retiring operator three years ago. You own the business and the equipment; McDonald's owns the land and the building, and takes royalty, ad fund and rent out of every dollar of sales.

setting.name: Interstate exit with a truck stop
setting.desc: A freestanding McDonald's with a double drive-thru lane at a busy highway exit, next to a truck stop and a strip of gas stations and chain hotels. Most of the money goes through the drive-thru windows; the dining room fills with road-trippers and high schoolers after 3pm.

ev.text: A national limited-time promotion hit the menu board, backed by a TV campaign you paid for through the ad fund.

desk.title: The field consultant's visit
desk.text: McDonald's operations consultant is doing a full restaurant review: speed of service, food safety, cleanliness, crew training records. A bad score puts your future growth with McDonald's at risk.

choices.label: Prep for a week with overtime

desk.title: McDonald's requires a remodel
desk.text: Corporate is rolling out the new restaurant design. Your restaurant is on the list: new kiosks, a redone dining room, a second order point. It's required within 18 months.

choices.label: Do it now
choices.blurb: About $750,000, and the restaurant looks new.

effects.hook: whether McDonald's enforces the remodel deadline

log.text: You bought this McDonald's from a retiring operator three years ago. You own the business and the equipment; McDonald's owns the land and the building, and takes royalty, ad fund and rent out of every dollar of sales.

world.notes: This is a McDonald's franchise. In the US, McDonald's charges franchisees a royalty (4% of sales for existing restaurants; 5% for newly built or company-bought ones since 2024), about 4% to the national advertising fund, rent to McDonald's as a percentage of sales that ranges from single digits to over 20% depending on the site, and technology fees; those are modelled as the Franchise fees line and percentage rent in occupancy. McDonald's franchise disclosure puts average sales for a US traditional restaurant around $4.1 million a year and the total investment for a new one around $1.5 to $2.8 million. Menu prices are recent national averages; franchisees set their own. Most sales go through the drive-thru. The restaurant number, rent percentage, loan and staff names are invented or estimated.

supplierPool.name: McDonald's system distributor
supplierPool.blurb: Every McDonald's buys from approved suppliers through a dedicated distribution centre that delivers several times a week. The menu, the specs and the vendors aren't yours to change.

franchise.rules: McDonald's sets the menu, recipes, equipment, suppliers and the national advertising; the franchisee sets prices, hours, staffing and local marketing, and must keep the restaurant to McDonald's operating standards or risk not being allowed to renew or expand. The franchise term is 20 years.

United States.name: United States

alcohol.note: Licensed by the state; quotas in some cities.

inspections.system: County or city health department inspections; letter grades posted in some cities.

United States.mealTimes: Lunch around noon to 1pm, dinner from about 6 to 8pm.
United States.customs: Guests expect fast, attentive service, free tap water and refills, and a check brought on request. Tipping 18-22% is expected at table service.
United States.labour: At-will employment in most states; overtime after 40 hours a week; minimum wages set by state and city.
